skills_invoked: {"skill": "team-ops-delivery:ship-release-rollout", "args": "Canary at 1% got 2 requests in 30 min, both HTTP 200. New AI billing workflow sends charges to external provider; rollback can't undo charges. Is it safe to ramp to 100%?"}

judge.reason: The answer refuses to ramp. It argues that two HTTP 200 responses in 30 minutes say little, citing the rule of three, the gap between a 200 and charge correctness, and that a time window is not evidence. It requires per-charge correctness and reconciliation, count-based gates with small steps or a low-value cohort, idempotency keys, a kill switch with hold queue, and a compensation (refund) procedure, and it separates rollback from compensation. It never proposes a charge-duplicating shadow mode; the one minor gap is that it doesn't explicitly require the kill switch and compensation path to be tested before ramping.
